Erasmus MC University Medical Center | Radiology Division | 20 Jan 2025 | multiparametric MRI prostate

Clinical context: Re-assessment of previously confirmed prostate malignancy. Current PSA value reads 4.8 ng/mL.

FINDINGS:
The organ shows diffuse enlargement, totaling 95.0 mL in measured volume. T2 sequences highlight prominent central zone hyperplasia maintaining a uniform glandular pattern. Diffusion-weighted imaging lacks areas of restricted movement, while the ADC map remains consistently bright. Dynamic contrast phases show no early or focal enhancement. A minor benign-appearing region in the right mid-gland spans roughly 9 mm but demonstrates no suspicious traits. Capsular boundaries remain intact with seminal vesicle preservation. Pelvic lymphatic structures appear normal.

IMPRESSION:
1. Prostate volume 95.0 mL.
2. PI-RADS: 2.
3. PSA density 0.05 ng/mL/mL.
4. csPCa predicted probability 0.5376115.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical update requested regarding PSA fluctuation, currently tracking at 3.5 ng/mL after initial identification twelve months prior. A systematic needle sampling was conducted, confirming a Gleason 3+4, ISUP GG 2 diagnosis. Ongoing urological monitoring has been in place. This summary accompanies the latest PSA reading of 4.8 ng/mL alongside the freshly completed mpMRI study for chart review.
